name: Manual Dexterity
definition: The ability to quickly move your hand, your hand together with your arm, or your two hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects.

benchmark.name: Robotic Grasping and Manipulation Competition
benchmark.model_or_system: Team SDU (University of Southern Denmark) autonomous assembly workstation
benchmark.metric: competition points (273 task points maximum, plus a time bonus)
benchmark.human_reference: Median manufacturing assembly worker or typical adult doing hand assembly of small mechanical and electrical parts (pegs, gears, connectors, nuts)

benchmark.name: D4RL
benchmark.metric: D4RL normalized score (0 = random policy, 100 = expert policy), reported per task

benchmark.name: MyoChallenge
benchmark.model_or_system: Team stiff_finger (PPO-LSTM with a curriculum, final ensemble of policies), Baoding Balls track, Phase 2
benchmark.metric: percent (the challenge's task score, i.e. share of evaluation episodes solved; effort, 0.03, was a secondary measure)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday manual dexterity tasks (in-hand manipulation and object rotation), not specialists such as surgeons or watchmakers

benchmark.name: ManiSkill2
benchmark.metric: average success rate (%) across the challenge's rigid-body test tasks
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce doing routine manual handling and assembly work, such as assemblers, warehouse and production workers. Their typical level of manual dexterity is the reference.

benchmark.name: FurnitureBench
benchmark.model_or_system: DPPO (Diffusion Policy Policy Optimization), trained in simulation and transferred zero-shot to a real Franka robot
benchmark.metric: task success rate (%) on real-world FurnitureBench One-leg assembly, 20 hardware trials
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing manual assembly (e.g., assembly or warehouse workers, typical adults assembling flat-pack furniture)

benchmark.name: RoboTwin 2.0
benchmark.metric: average success rate (%) over the 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, randomized setting
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday two-handed manual handling (e.g., warehouse, assembly-line, or service workers)

benchmark.name: ManipulationNet
benchmark.model_or_system: InsertAnything (RL insertion policy trained only in simulation, using fingertip force feedback)
benchmark.metric: percent of the 20 ManipulationNet peg-in-hole tasks completed (5 hole shapes × 4 clearance levels); reported as 20/20
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / manual assembly workforce (typical assembler or technician doing hand insertion and fitting of parts)
